title: Financial Accounting I
topics: Final accounts of a sole trader
Nature and purpose of financial accounting

items.q: A machine costing 240000 naira has an expected value of 60000 naira at the end of its life of 4 years. What is the yearly charge using the straight line method?
items.s: Yearly charge = (cost - end value)/life = (240000 - 60000)/4 = 45000 naira.

items.q: A trader has receivables of 720000 naira. A customer who owes 38000 naira is declared unable to pay and the amount is written off. What figure for receivables remains?
items.s: Remaining receivables = 720000 - 38000 = 682000 naira.

items.q: Goods with a list price of 480000 naira are sold subject to a trade discount of 5 percent. What is the amount charged to the customer?
items.s: Amount charged = list price x (100 - discount)/100 = 480000 x (100 - 5)/100 = 456000 naira.

items.q: Opening stock was 95000 naira, purchases were 240000 naira and closing stock was 105000 naira. What is the cost of the goods sold?
items.s: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock = 95000 + 240000 - 105000 = 230000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Sales for the year were 620000 naira and the cost of the goods sold was 410000 naira. What is the gross profit?
items.s: Gross profit = sales - cost of goods sold = 620000 - 410000 = 210000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Goods costing 180000 naira are to be sold at a mark-up of 20 percent on cost. What is the selling price?
items.s: Selling price = cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 180000 x (100 + 20)/100 = 216000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A petty cash float of 25000 naira is reimbursed at the end of the month when 4650 naira is left in the box. How much is paid back into the float?
items.s: Reimbursement = float - cash left = 25000 - 4650 = 20350 naira.

items.q: The debit column of a trial balance totals 320000 naira and the credit column totals 307000 naira. What amount is carried to the suspense account?
items.s: Suspense = difference between the two columns = 320000 - 307000 = 13000 naira.

items.q: Equipment costing 300000 naira is expected to be worth 50000 naira after 8 years and is written off evenly. What is the total charged against profit after 3 years?
items.s: Total charge = years x (cost - end value)/life = 3 x (300000 - 50000)/8 = 93750 naira.

items.q: A vehicle costing 750000 naira has a scrap value of 80000 naira and a life of 10 years and is written off evenly. What amount is carried in the books after 4 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost - years x (cost - scrap)/life = 750000 - 4 x (750000 - 80000)/10 = 482000 naira.

items.q: An asset is bought for 350000 naira and is written down at 15 percent each year on the reducing balance. What is the charge for the first year?
items.s: First year charge = cost x rate = 350000 x 15/100 = 52500 naira.

items.q: A plant costing 625000 naira is written down at 20 percent each year on the reducing balance. What amount is carried in the books at the end of 2 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost x (1 - rate/100)^years = 625000 x (1 - 20/100)^2 = 400000 naira.

items.q: An asset bought for 720000 naira has been written down by 240000 naira. It is now sold for 520000 naira. What is the gain on the sale?
items.s: Gain = proceeds - amount carried = 520000 - (720000 - 240000) = 40000 naira.

items.q: Rent paid during the year was 300000 naira. Rent owing at the start of the year was 30000 naira and rent owing at the end was 55000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + closing amount owing - opening amount owing = 300000 + 55000 - 30000 = 325000 naira.

items.q: Insurance paid during the year was 210000 naira. Insurance paid in advance at the start of the year was 27000 naira and at the end it was 54000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + opening amount in advance - closing amount in advance = 210000 + 27000 - 54000 = 183000 naira.

items.q: Interest received during the year was 210000 naira. Interest due at the start of the year was 32000 naira and interest due at the end was 58000 naira. What is the income for the year?
items.s: Income = amount received - opening amount due + closing amount due = 210000 - 32000 + 58000 = 236000 naira.

items.q: Trade receivables at the year end are 480000 naira. A provision of 5 percent is to be made against them. What is the amount of the provision?
items.s: Provision = receivables x rate/100 = 480000 x 5/100 = 24000 naira.

items.q: The provision against doubtful debts stood at 22000 naira at the start of the year and is to be 66000 naira at the end. What amount is charged against profit for the year?
items.s: Charge = closing provision - opening provision = 66000 - 22000 = 44000 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units that cost 10 naira each and then bought 300 units at 24 naira each. 350 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the cost of the units issued?
items.s: Under FIFO the issue is priced from the oldest units: 200 x 10 + 150 x 24 = 5600 naira.

items.q: A store held 300 units costing 20 naira each and bought 200 units costing 24 naira each. What is the weighted average cost per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = total cost/total units = (300 x 20 + 200 x 24)/(300 + 200) = 21.6 naira.

items.q: Goods that cost 180000 naira can be sold for 200000 naira after spending 50000 naira to finish them and 18000 naira to sell them. At what amount should they be carried?
items.s: Net realisable value = 200000 - 50000 - 18000 = 132000; stock is carried at the lower of 180000 and 132000, which is 132000 naira.

items.q: Purchases for the year were 320000 naira, carriage inwards was 18000 naira and returns outwards were 31000 naira. What figure is shown for net purchases?
items.s: Net purchases = purchases + carriage inwards - returns outwards = 320000 + 18000 - 31000 = 307000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Gross profit was 180000 naira, other income was 16000 naira and the expenses of the period were 162000 naira. What is the net profit?
items.s: Net profit = gross profit + other income - expenses = 180000 + 16000 - 162000 = 34000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A trader earns a gross profit of 25 percent on selling price. What is the mark-up on cost?
items.s: Mark-up = margin/(100 - margin) x 100 = 25/(100 - 25) x 100 = 33.33 percent.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Capital at the start of the year was 700000 naira, profit for the year was 210000 naira and capital at the end was 780000 naira. What were the drawings?
items.s: Drawings = opening capital + profit - closing capital = 700000 + 210000 - 780000 = 130000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A bank statement shows a credit balance of 615000 naira. Deposits of 38000 naira have not been credited and cheques of 47000 naira have not been presented. What is the corrected cash book balance?
items.s: Corrected balance = statement balance + uncredited deposits - unpresented cheques = 615000 + 38000 - 47000 = 606000 naira.

items.q: The receivables control account opens with a debit balance of 95000 naira. Credit sales were 495000 naira, receipts from customers were 340000 naira and returns inwards were 12000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + credit sales - receipts - returns = 95000 + 495000 - 340000 - 12000 = 238000 naira.

items.q: The payables control account opens with a credit balance of 148000 naira. Credit purchases were 425000 naira, payments to suppliers were 350000 naira and returns outwards were 15000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + credit purchases - payments - returns = 148000 + 425000 - 350000 - 15000 = 208000 naira.

items.s: Capital = assets - liabilities = 180000 - 135000 = 45000 naira.

items.q: capital may be defined as
o: a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood
the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
items.s: capital: the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations. The other options describe aged list of balances, purchases ledger control, accrued income.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines straight line.
o: an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
income earned from the ordinary trading activity of the business
the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
items.s: straight line: the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset. The other options describe profit and loss account, purchases ledger control, Revenue.

items.q: Which term is described by “the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses”?
o: error of original entry
trial balance
debit
credit
items.s: debit is the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses.

items.q: The statement “the estimated selling price less the costs still to be incurred and the costs of selling” describes which of the following?
o: net realisable value
residual value
reducing balance
provision for depreciation
items.s: net realisable value is the estimated selling price less the costs still to be incurred and the costs of selling.

items.q: Which term is described by “the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations”?
o: trading account
gross profit
capital
working capital
items.s: capital is the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: materiality may be defined as
o: the rule that stock is carried at whichever of the two amounts is smaller
the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts
the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
a statement of assets, liabilities and capital at a stated date
items.s: materiality: the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure. The other options describe complete reversal, Statement of financial position, lower of cost and net realisable value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes inventory count?
o: the process of inserting the figure that makes the two sides of an account agree
the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts
the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
items.s: inventory count: the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end. The other options describe complete reversal, balancing off, straight line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines weighted average?
o: an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
the convention that treats the owner and the firm as two separate parties for record keeping
the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
the method that divides the total cost of goods available by the total quantity available
items.s: weighted average: the method that divides the total cost of goods available by the total quantity available. The other options describe accrued expense, business entity, profit and loss account.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines trade discount.
o: money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises
the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
items.s: trade discount: a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer. The other options describe profit and loss account, control account, income received in advance.

items.q: The statement “the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed” describes which of the following?
o: realisation
going concern
accrual basis
historical cost
items.s: realisation is the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed.

items.q: Which of the following best describes materiality?
o: the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn
items.s: materiality: the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure. The other options describe matching, error of omission, accrued income.

items.q: The statement “money collected before the service to which it relates has been given” describes which of the following?
o: lower of cost and net realisable value
income received in advance
straight line
fifo
items.s: income received in advance is money collected before the service to which it relates has been given.

items.q: Which term is described by “the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned”?
o: receipt
purchases returns book
invoice
credit note
items.s: credit note is the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines capital?
o: the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
items.s: capital: the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations. The other options describe straight line, standing order, discount allowed.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: The statement “the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float” describes which of the following?
o: receipt
petty cash voucher
sales day book
journal proper
items.s: petty cash voucher is the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float.

items.q: Which term is described by “money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it”?
o: reducing balance
inventory count
depreciation
accrued income
items.s: accrued income is money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it.

items.q: Which of the following best describes income received in advance?
o: the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
items.s: income received in advance: money collected before the service to which it relates has been given. The other options describe error of original entry, sales day book, contra set off.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines aged list of balances.
o: a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood
items.s: aged list of balances: a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood. The other options describe prepayment, reducing balance, trade discount.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines income received in advance.
o: an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited
money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
items.s: income received in advance: money collected before the service to which it relates has been given. The other options describe capital, unpresented cheque, purchases ledger control.

items.q: Which of the following best describes prepayment?
o: the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
the duty of management to account to the owners for resources entrusted to them
an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
items.s: prepayment: an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period. The other options describe reducing balance, debit note, Stewardship.

items.q: The statement “the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain” describes which of the following?
o: consistency
prudence
realisation
going concern
items.s: prudence is the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain.

items.q: Which of the following best describes net book value?
o: the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float
a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay
the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date
items.s: net book value: the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date. The other options describe petty cash voucher, provision for doubtful debts, capital.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines provision for depreciation.
o: the excess of revenue over the expenses incurred in earning it
the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected
the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
items.s: provision for depreciation: the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought. The other options describe reducing balance, posting, Profit.

items.q: Which term is described by “the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves”?
o: lower of cost and net realisable value
depreciation
net book value
prepayment
items.s: depreciation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Capital.
o: the owner's interest in the business, being assets less liabilities
the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date
the principal book of account in which transactions are classified under account headings
a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited
items.s: Capital: the owner's interest in the business, being assets less liabilities. The other options describe ledger, unpresented cheque, net book value.
items.t: Nature and purpose of financial accounting

items.q: Which of the following best describes receipt?
o: a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited
the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses
the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly
items.s: receipt: the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received. The other options describe debit, discount received, unpresented cheque.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines discount allowed.
o: two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
the process of inserting the figure that makes the two sides of an account agree
a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly
the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected
items.s: discount allowed: a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly. The other options describe posting, compensating error, balancing off.

items.q: compensating error may be defined as
o: an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
items.s: compensating error: two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out. The other options describe error of original entry, prepayment, income received in advance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes error of omission?
o: money or goods taken by the owner for personal use
amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
items.s: error of omission: the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees. The other options describe accrued income, bank charges, Drawings.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines error of omission.
o: the convention of carrying assets at the amount paid to acquire them
the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
items.s: error of omission: the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees. The other options describe prudence, historical cost, profit and loss account.

items.q: Which term is described by “amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send”?
o: bank reconciliation statement
unpresented cheque
bank charges
standing order

income received in advance
prepayment
reducing balance

credit note
purchases returns book
petty cash voucher

items.q: Which statement correctly defines consistency?

the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next
the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected
items.s: consistency: the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next. The other options describe credit note, posting, credit.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines working capital?
o: the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year
the duty of management to account to the owners for resources entrusted to them
the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn
items.s: working capital: the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year. The other options describe residual value, matching, Stewardship.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines compensating error?

the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first
two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next

items.q: The statement “money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use” describes which of the following?

gross profit
capital
drawings

items.q: going concern may be defined as
o: an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books
the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future
the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer
a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced
items.s: going concern: the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future. The other options describe suspense account, bad debt, invoice.

items.q: Which term is described by “an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals”?
o: standing order
bank reconciliation statement
unpresented cheque
uncredited deposit

items.q: Which of the following best describes depreciation?
o: the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves
the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
items.s: depreciation: the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves. The other options describe reducing balance, residual value, error of original entry.

items.q: Which term is described by “an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books”?
o: aged list of balances
bad debt
trade discount
discount allowed

items.q: Which statement correctly defines error of principle?

the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse
the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float
the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
items.s: error of principle: the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse. The other options describe petty cash voucher, capital, standing order.

items.q: Which of the following best describes profit and loss account?

the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
the routine recording of transactions before any reporting is done
the statement that shows the gross result of buying and selling goods

items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines debit.
o: the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
items.s: debit: the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses. The other options describe purchases ledger control, straight line, sales day book.

items.q: Which term is described by “a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay”?
o: discount received
discount allowed
provision for doubtful debts
sales ledger control
items.s: provision for doubtful debts is a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines error of commission.
o: the routine recording of transactions before any reporting is done
the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
items.s: error of commission: the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person. The other options describe Bookkeeping, purchases returns book, credit note.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines journal proper?

income earned from the ordinary trading activity of the business
the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float
the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books

items.q: Which term is described by “the process of inserting the figure that makes the two sides of an account agree”?

compensating error
suspense account
balancing off

the statement that shows the gross result of buying and selling goods
money paid in by the firm that the bank has not yet added to the account

money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use

control account
discount received
bad debt

the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income

the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
an account that totals the transactions with all credit customers
an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books

items.q: Which term is described by “the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse”?
o: error of original entry
error of principle
error of omission
credit

recording past transactions and reporting them to owners and other outsiders
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
the excess of revenue over the expenses incurred in earning it

a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay

a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it

a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises
the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts

items.q: A plant costing 400000 naira is written down at 25 percent each year on the reducing balance. What amount is carried in the books at the end of 4 years?

items.q: Goods that cost 180000 naira can be sold for 200000 naira after spending 20000 naira to finish them and 26000 naira to sell them. At what amount should they be carried?

items.q: Rent paid during the year was 120000 naira. Rent owing at the start of the year was 10000 naira and rent owing at the end was 55000 naira. What is the charge for the year?

items.q: Interest received during the year was 140000 naira. Interest due at the start of the year was 12000 naira and interest due at the end was 45000 naira. What is the income for the year?

items.q: A store held 300 units that cost 12 naira each and then bought 300 units at 18 naira each. 400 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the cost of the units issued?

items.q: Opening stock was 95000 naira, purchases were 240000 naira and closing stock was 55000 naira. What is the cost of the goods sold?

items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Purchases for the year were 455000 naira, carriage inwards was 34000 naira and returns outwards were 22000 naira. What figure is shown for net purchases?

items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Gross profit was 245000 naira, other income was 16000 naira and the expenses of the period were 128000 naira. What is the net profit?
items.s: Net profit = gross profit + other income - expenses = 245000 + 16000 - 128000 = 133000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: The payables control account opens with a credit balance of 105000 naira. Credit purchases were 310000 naira, payments to suppliers were 260000 naira and returns outwards were 15000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + credit purchases - payments - returns = 105000 + 310000 - 260000 - 15000 = 140000 naira.

items.q: A petty cash float of 30000 naira is reimbursed at the end of the month when 4650 naira is left in the box. How much is paid back into the float?
items.s: Reimbursement = float - cash left = 30000 - 4650 = 25350 naira.

items.q: A vehicle costing 480000 naira has a scrap value of 30000 naira and a life of 6 years and is written off evenly. What amount is carried in the books after 4 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost - years x (cost - scrap)/life = 480000 - 4 x (480000 - 30000)/6 = 180000 naira.

items.q: An asset bought for 560000 naira has been written down by 240000 naira. It is now sold for 360000 naira. What is the gain on the sale?
items.s: Gain = proceeds - amount carried = 360000 - (560000 - 240000) = 40000 naira.

items.q: Insurance paid during the year was 150000 naira. Insurance paid in advance at the start of the year was 27000 naira and at the end it was 42000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + opening amount in advance - closing amount in advance = 150000 + 27000 - 42000 = 135000 naira.

items.q: A store held 300 units costing 16 naira each and bought 100 units costing 30 naira each. What is the weighted average cost per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = total cost/total units = (300 x 16 + 100 x 30)/(300 + 100) = 19.5 naira.

items.q: Goods that cost 250000 naira can be sold for 200000 naira after spending 50000 naira to finish them and 18000 naira to sell them. At what amount should they be carried?

items.q: The receivables control account opens with a debit balance of 130000 naira. Credit sales were 560000 naira, receipts from customers were 210000 naira and returns inwards were 19000 naira. What is the closing balance?

items.q: The debit column of a trial balance totals 465000 naira and the credit column totals 444000 naira. What amount is carried to the suspense account?

items.q: A machine costing 240000 naira has an expected value of 40000 naira at the end of its life of 5 years. What is the yearly charge using the straight line method?

items.q: Equipment costing 600000 naira is expected to be worth 30000 naira after 6 years and is written off evenly. What is the total charged against profit after 2 years?
items.s: Total charge = years x (cost - end value)/life = 2 x (600000 - 30000)/6 = 190000 naira.

items.q: An asset is bought for 200000 naira and is written down at 25 percent each year on the reducing balance. What is the charge for the first year?

items.q: A plant costing 500000 naira is written down at 10 percent each year on the reducing balance. What amount is carried in the books at the end of 4 years?

items.q: Interest received during the year was 140000 naira. Interest due at the start of the year was 32000 naira and interest due at the end was 74000 naira. What is the income for the year?

items.q: A trader has receivables of 465000 naira. A customer who owes 38000 naira is declared unable to pay and the amount is written off. What figure for receivables remains?

items.q: Trade receivables at the year end are 360000 naira. A provision of 5 percent is to be made against them. What is the amount of the provision?

items.q: Goods with a list price of 200000 naira are sold subject to a trade discount of 5 percent. What is the amount charged to the customer?

items.q: A store held 100 units that cost 12 naira each and then bought 300 units at 18 naira each. 200 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the cost of the units issued?

items.q: Goods costing 120000 naira are to be sold at a mark-up of 25 percent on cost. What is the selling price?

items.q: A bank statement shows a credit balance of 740000 naira. Deposits of 52000 naira have not been credited and cheques of 31000 naira have not been presented. What is the corrected cash book balance?

items.q: The payables control account opens with a credit balance of 72000 naira. Credit purchases were 310000 naira, payments to suppliers were 260000 naira and returns outwards were 23000 naira. What is the closing balance?

items.q: The provision against doubtful debts stood at 30000 naira at the start of the year and is to be 52000 naira at the end. What amount is charged against profit for the year?

items.q: A store held 400 units costing 12 naira each and bought 300 units costing 30 naira each. What is the weighted average cost per unit?

items.q: A firm has total assets of 265000 naira and total liabilities of 135000 naira. What is the capital of the owner?

items.q: Which of the following best describes residual value?
o: the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first
the ledger record used to work out the gain or loss when an asset leaves the firm
items.s: residual value: the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use. The other options describe provision for depreciation, disposal account, fifo.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties”
o: aged list of balances
trade discount
contra set off
sales ledger control
items.s: contra set off is the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sales day book?
o: the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float
items.s: sales day book: the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger. The other options describe petty cash voucher, debit note, invoice.

items.q: inventory count may be defined as
o: the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn
the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
the estimated selling price less the costs still to be incurred and the costs of selling
items.s: inventory count: the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end. The other options describe reducing balance, matching, net realisable value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes debit note?
o: the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
items.s: debit note: the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill. The other options describe credit note, journal proper, receipt.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines error of omission?
o: two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
the principal book of account in which transactions are classified under account headings
the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
items.s: error of omission: the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees. The other options describe compensating error, ledger, credit.

items.q: Which term is described by “a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood”?
o: sales ledger control
aged list of balances
discount received
discount allowed
items.s: aged list of balances is a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood.

items.q: bank reconciliation statement may be defined as
o: a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers
a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send
items.s: bank reconciliation statement: a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers. The other options describe unpresented cheque, standing order, bank charges.

items.q: bad debt may be defined as
o: a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly
an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books
a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises
an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
items.s: bad debt: an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books. The other options describe purchases ledger control, discount allowed, control account.

items.q: realisation may be defined as
o: the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain
the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
items.s: realisation: the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed. The other options describe going concern, prudence, materiality.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Profit.
o: income earned from the ordinary trading activity of the business
the owner's interest in the business, being assets less liabilities
the excess of revenue over the expenses incurred in earning it
the duty of management to account to the owners for resources entrusted to them
items.s: Profit: the excess of revenue over the expenses incurred in earning it. The other options describe Capital, Revenue, Stewardship.

items.q: Which term is described by “the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger”?
o: sales day book
invoice
debit note
petty cash voucher
items.s: sales day book is the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger.

items.q: credit may be defined as
o: the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts
the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income
the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
items.s: credit: the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income. The other options describe error of commission, error of original entry, complete reversal.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines capital.
o: the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
the difference between the sales value of goods and what those goods cost the trader
the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year
items.s: capital: the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations. The other options describe profit and loss account, gross profit, working capital.

items.q: Which of the following best describes unpresented cheque?
o: money paid in by the firm that the bank has not yet added to the account
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited
a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers
items.s: unpresented cheque: a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited. The other options describe uncredited deposit, bank reconciliation statement, standing order.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the owner's interest in the business, being assets less liabilities”

Revenue
Statement of financial position
Bookkeeping
items.s: Capital is the owner's interest in the business, being assets less liabilities.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines suspense account.
o: the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced
the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected
items.s: suspense account: a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced. The other options describe error of omission, complete reversal, posting.

items.q: discount allowed is best described as
o: an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books
a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly
an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
items.s: discount allowed: a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly. The other options describe bad debt, purchases ledger control, trade discount.

items.q: consignment stock may be defined as
o: the ledger record used to work out the gain or loss when an asset leaves the firm
goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold
money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date
items.s: consignment stock: goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold. The other options describe income received in advance, disposal account, net book value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes prudence?
o: the convention that treats the owner and the firm as two separate parties for record keeping
the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain
the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next
the convention of carrying assets at the amount paid to acquire them
items.s: prudence: the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain. The other options describe consistency, historical cost, business entity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes journal proper?
o: the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
items.s: journal proper: the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books. The other options describe debit note, sales day book, receipt.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines provision for doubtful debts?
o: a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood
a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay
items.s: provision for doubtful debts: a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay. The other options describe purchases ledger control, aged list of balances, trade discount.

items.q: consistency may be defined as
o: the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next
the convention of carrying assets at the amount paid to acquire them
items.s: consistency: the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next. The other options describe historical cost, realisation, materiality.

items.q: Which term is described by “the convention that treats the owner and the firm as two separate parties for record keeping”?
o: materiality
prudence
business entity
accrual basis
items.s: business entity is the convention that treats the owner and the firm as two separate parties for record keeping.

items.q: trial balance may be defined as
o: the principal book of account in which transactions are classified under account headings
the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts
a list of ledger balances taken out to check that total left side amounts equal total right side amounts
items.s: trial balance: a list of ledger balances taken out to check that total left side amounts equal total right side amounts. The other options describe double entry, error of commission, ledger.

items.q: credit note may be defined as
o: the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
items.s: credit note: the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned. The other options describe petty cash voucher, journal proper, receipt.

items.q: Which term is described by “the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year”?
o: capital
drawings
trading account
working capital
items.s: working capital is the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year.

recording income and expenses in the period they are earned or incurred rather than when money moves
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future
items.s: going concern: the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future. The other options describe accrual basis, business entity, realisation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes historical cost?
o: the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future
the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
the convention of carrying assets at the amount paid to acquire them
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
items.s: historical cost: the convention of carrying assets at the amount paid to acquire them. The other options describe realisation, materiality, going concern.

the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next
the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
items.s: going concern: the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future. The other options describe realisation, consistency, materiality.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date”
o: net realisable value
accrued expense
residual value
net book value
items.s: net book value is the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the difference between the sales value of goods and what those goods cost the trader”

capital
profit and loss account

the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses

the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations

items.s: credit: the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income. The other options describe complete reversal, error of omission, error of original entry.

the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first
an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves
items.s: accrued expense: an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it. The other options describe fifo, consignment stock, depreciation.

o: credit
debit
error of omission
error of original entry
items.s: error of omission is the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees.

the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations

matching
